descriptionChirho: Adjective describing holiness as an intrinsic attribute of God or as a quality predicated of persons/things, used predicatively or attributively in the singular.
Substantivized singular adjective used as a divine title, especially in the construct phrase 'the Holy One of Israel' (qedosh Yisra'el), referring to God as the uniquely set-apart one.
Substantivized plural adjective referring to holy beings — either angelic beings in the divine council or human saints/faithful ones set apart for God.
Substantivized plural used in construct to denote sacred or consecrated objects, offerings, or items dedicated to God.
Used in construct to refer to a sacred place or the quality of sanctity associated with a location, as in 'the holy place of' a deity.
